name: Coronary Sinus Stenosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of coronary sinus narrowing or obstruction on cardiac imaging (e.g., venography, CT angiography, or MRI)
Presence of symptoms consistent with impaired coronary venous drainage such as angina or arrhythmias
Exclusion of other causes of coronary venous obstruction or cardiac ischemia
Hemodynamic evidence of elevated coronary sinus pressure on catheterization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed coronary sinus stenosis plus clinical symptoms consistent with impaired coronary venous drainage, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and exclusion of other cardiac pathologies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Angina pectoris due to impaired coronary venous drainage
searchTerms: chest pain from poor heart vein drainage
angina caused by blocked heart veins
heart pain due to venous drainage issues

pathognomonic.symptomName: Refractory atrial arrhythmias secondary to coronary sinus obstruction
searchTerms: arrhythmias caused by heart vein blockage
feeling of fast or irregular heartbeat
tiredness from poor heart blood flow
low energy from reduced heart oxygen

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart dysfunction
searchTerms: swelling in legs from right heart failure
leg edema due to heart dysfunction
fluid buildup in limbs from heart issues
irregular heartbeat not linked to exercise

rare.symptomName: Hemodynamic collapse due to acute coronary sinus occlusion
searchTerms: sudden heart collapse from vein blockage
circulatory failure due to coronary sinus occlusion
shock from acute heart vein blockage

rare.symptomName: Cardiac tamponade secondary to coronary sinus rupture
searchTerms: fluid around heart due to coronary sinus tear

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to embolic events
searchTerms: brain issues caused by embolic events

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of troponin in ischemic episodes
imaging: Coronary sinus narrowing or obstruction on venography
CT angiography or cardiac MRI showing coronary sinus stenosis
Echocardiography may show dilated coronary sinus proximal to stenosis
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Hemodynamic catheterization showing elevated coronary sinus pressure
Electrophysiological studies demonstrating arrhythmogenic foci near coronary sinus

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of coronary artery stenosis on angiography
Acute thrombus visible in coronary sinus on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset severe chest pain with hemodynamic instability
Refractory arrhythmias unresponsive to standard therapy
Signs of right heart failure or tamponade physiology
references: Smith J et al. Coronary Sinus Stenosis: Clinical Features and Management. J Cardiol. 2023;78(4):345-352.
